headlines.title: European Gas Prices Rise Above €90 for First Time Since 2022
headlines.summary: European natgas cracking €90 for the first time since the 2022 energy crisis is a five-alarm fire for the continent — it hits utilities, industrials, and chemicals hard while feeding the inflation narrative that keeps the ECB's hands tied. Layer in the France unrest and Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure, and you've got a supply-shock cocktail that moves the long bond, the euro, and energy equities simultaneously. This is the kind of tape-changer that makes every other story this morning look like noise.

headlines.title: French unrest compounds debt crisis fears. Paris-listed stocks, bonds and the euro fall
headlines.summary: When the people riot AND the bond market riots at the same time, you've got a genuine sovereign stress event — and France is the eurozone's second-largest economy, so this isn't some peripheral sideshow. OAT spreads widening, the CAC getting shorted aggressively, and the euro under pressure all feed back into U.S. multinationals with European exposure and risk-off flows globally. The ECB is caught flat-footed between supporting growth and defending fiscal credibility, which is exactly the kind of policy paralysis markets hate.

headlines.title: South Korean IPO flop is the latest in a string of disappointments for the global AI trade
headlines.summary: Three data-center IPOs shelved in October alone — backed by Nvidia, Blackstone, and SoftBank — and now Elice faceplants on debut: the market is sending a loud message that it's done writing blank checks for AI capex stories without a clear return on investment. This hits the entire neocloud complex, pressures hyperscaler valuations ahead of a critical earnings week, and validates the Gartner note that sparked last week's tech rout. Watch NVDA, SMCI, and the broader QQQ — the bid under this trade is shakier than the bulls want to admit.
